questions.question: Which finding most strongly requires emergency evaluation for possible cauda equina syndrome?
choices: New urinary retention with saddle anesthesia and bilateral progressive weakness
Stable chronic mechanical back pain
Pain improved by brief activity
A routine request for physical therapy
questions.explanation: New bladder dysfunction, saddle anesthesia, and progressive bilateral weakness can indicate cauda equina syndrome and require emergency evaluation.

questions.question: When is routine imaging generally not recommended for acute low back pain?
choices: When there are no focal neurologic deficits or red flags for serious pathology
When progressive weakness is present
When infection is suspected
When major trauma raises fracture concern
questions.explanation: Routine imaging does not improve outcomes in uncomplicated acute low back pain without focal deficits or serious-condition red flags.

questions.question: Which pattern can suggest lumbar spinal stenosis?
choices: Walking/standing limitation relieved by flexion or sitting
Sudden urinary retention
A febrile patient with bacteremia
Immediate pain after a single skin rash
questions.explanation: Neurogenic claudication from spinal stenosis is often worsened by walking/standing and relieved by flexion or sitting.

questions.question: What should a focused low back pain examination include?
choices: Gait, strength, sensation, reflexes, relevant provocation, hips, and systemic findings
Only a pain score
Only a lumbar x-ray
Only body weight
questions.explanation: A focused neurologic and musculoskeletal examination helps identify deficits, alternatives, and urgency.

questions.question: Why is imaging stewardship important in uncomplicated low back pain?
choices: Routine imaging can reveal incidental findings and does not usually improve outcomes
Imaging always prevents chronic pain
Pain severity alone requires MRI
Imaging replaces return precautions
questions.explanation: Unnecessary imaging can cause cost, anxiety, incidental findings, and downstream intervention without improving uncomplicated acute pain outcomes.

questions.question: What is an appropriate management focus for nonspecific low back pain without red flags?
choices: Functional goals, activity within tolerance, education, and individualized nonpharmacologic options
Prolonged bed rest
Immediate opioid therapy for every patient
Ignoring sleep and work limitations
questions.explanation: Functional recovery and active, individualized nonpharmacologic care are central to nonspecific low back pain management.

questions.question: Why should psychosocial factors be assessed in persistent low back pain?
choices: They can influence disability, recovery, and treatment feasibility
They prove pain is not physical
They make examination unnecessary
They eliminate the need for red-flag screening
questions.explanation: Pain recovery is biopsychosocial; psychosocial factors can predict disability and guide supportive care without dismissing symptoms.

questions.question: Which is an important medication-safety action in low back pain care?
choices: Review kidney/GI/cardiovascular risk, interactions, sedation/fall risk, and OTC NSAID duplication
Use the same analgesic for every patient
Continue medications indefinitely without functional review
Ignore substance-use history
questions.explanation: Medication selection must be individualized and reviewed for comorbidity, interaction, functional benefit, and safety.

questions.question: What is an appropriate opioid-safety principle?
choices: Opioids are not a default treatment for nonspecific low back pain and should not be abruptly stopped by routine message
Every patient with back pain needs opioids
Abrupt discontinuation is always safest
Opioids replace functional rehabilitation
questions.explanation: Opioids have important risks and need careful, patient-centered assessment; abrupt discontinuation can cause harm.

questions.question: What is the FNP-level low back pain principle?
choices: Order MRI for every painful back
Screen for danger, use testing purposefully, and support functional recovery
Assume all pain is mechanical
Focus only on a medication refill
questions.explanation: High-quality care avoids missed emergencies and low-value testing while addressing recovery, function, and safety.
